items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Tony Pastor, who had taken over the leadership of Artie Shaw's orchestra when Artie split, came in a few times.

ctx.x: Quite a number of musicians were in the army on navy bands, and as salaries were going up in many jobs, we figured that it would be the right time to ask Barney for a raise. Barney told us that he thought we deserved one, but he didn't say he would give us one.

A few nights later, a guitarist named Gene Fields came to the Club, but we thought nothing of it because musicians came in often to see and listen to the musicians working there. Tony Pastor, who had taken over the leadership of Artie Shaw's orchestra when Artie split, came in a few times. Also, Lena Horne, when she was singing for a while with Charlie Barnet.

When we received the next pay check, there was a message in it, telling us that we had two more weeks in the Club. Barney thought that we deserved a raise, and he raised us out of the joint. Later, we learned that Gene Fields had replaced us, but we didn't hold any animosity towards Gene, because it was the same like it was played in the music field, and we still had a ball while we were at the Cafe Society Uptown.
